maria (sales): Charlie from Lark just pinged — for the Private POC they want to use their own KMS/HSM and need clear steps for credentials + certs. can we enumerate exactly what we need and who will action?

daniel (solutions): thanks — quick checklist idea: customer KMS access method (API creds / IAM role / HSM attestation), CA cert (or CSR flow), service account principal, network endpoints (vpc/subnet/cidr + allowed egress), and any ephemeral API key needs.

charlie (customer): yup, we prefer AWS CloudHSM and want minimal secrets handed to you. we can create an IAM role for cross-account access. also we require mTLS to the private control plane.

prasanna (infra): ok. for Cross-account KMS usage we need either: 1) an IAM role we assume with kms:Encrypt/Decrypt permissions (preferred), or 2) a short-lived client cert signed by your PKI for HSM proxy. which do you want to do?

charlie (customer): prefer role assumption. HSM admins want to avoid handing long-lived keys. role + mTLS sounds good.

maria (sales): noted. action owners: prasanna will draft required IAM policy + assume-role ARNs, daniel will prepare CSR + cert instructions, sarah will confirm this satisfies our security questionnaire items about key custody. charlie — we'll send a single doc with exact commands.

sarah (security): from the questionnaire POV we need: key separation details, key rotation cadence, attestations/certificates, audit log access, and whether Redwood holds any plaintext key material. answer: Redwood will not persist customer KMS key material; we use IAM assume-role and HSM signs inside customer's account. include that in the response.

daniel (solutions): drafting commands for the CSR + cert flow. if you need to sign a CSR yourself, this is what we expect:```
# generate private key and CSR
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out client.key -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -subj "/CN=redwood-poc-client/O=Lark" -out client.csr
```
Then paste the base64 CSR to us or return a signed cert. we can also accept a PEM chain.

charlie (customer): we can do that. do you need a particular CN or SAN?

daniel (solutions): prefer CN=redwood-poc-client and SAN with the service FQDN we'll provide. if you return a cert, include issuer chain and relayable trust anchor.

prasanna (infra): for IAM role we need these from your side: account-id, role name to assume, and a short-lived trust policy we provide. we'll also request these permissions: kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey on the key alias we will reference. sample policy snippet we will send in the doc.

maria (sales): pricing/POC note: since this is private with HSM access, POC run uses a small Dedicated pool + private control plane — addendum to POC quote to cover reserved infra for the window. I'll attach the revised estimate after infra confirms endpoints. :moneybag:

charlie (customer): who kicks off the private control plane install?

prasanna (infra): Redwood ops will coordinate. we need: bastion IPs (for management), allowed egress CIDR, and the signed client cert (or an SSM-like agent). we'll open a deployment window and send a runbook.

sarah (security): two compliance asks to confirm before we proceed: 1) will audit logs of KMS/HSM operations be forwarded to the customer's logging? 2) are we able to do periodic key rotation initiated by customer? answer both yes — include steps in the runbook.

charlie (customer): yes to both, we want CloudTrail forwarding and rotation by us with a staged fallback.

prasanna (infra): noted. for rotation we propose a dual-key rollout: new key alias -> verify decrypt on canary -> swap alias -> retire old key. we'll document CLI/API checks.

maria (sales): next steps: prasanna to post IAM policy + role trust template, daniel to post CSR example + expected cert metadata, sarah to draft the security Q response paragraph, and I'll update the POC quote. charlie — target to get those artifacts to you within 24h?

charlie (customer): that works. appreciate the clear owners.

deploy-bot: Certificate issuance record: request 1859120000 created, awaiting signed cert from customer.

daniel (solutions): sending doc link (draft): https://redwood.example/docs/poc/lark-private-kms-checklist — contains the policy snippets and CSR example. please review and comment.

prasanna (infra): I'll run the assume-role test once we have the role ARN. small note: if Lark wants HSM-backed keys but no cross-account role, we can also use an agent that proxies HSM calls from their VPC — that increases complexity, flagging now.

charlie (customer): we'll start with role assumption path. if we hit perf issues we'll consider the proxy.

maria (sales): great — I'll mark this thread as the POC credential thread for handoff to ops. will follow up with the revised estimate and calendar invite for deployment window. :white_check_mark:
